Method of Attack: Reprogramming the controller chip of a USB device to appear as a human interface device (HID) that can type and launch commands rapidly
Using a malicious USB charging cable that acts as a HID device to issue commands and compromise computers
Launching commands that download and execute payloads on unlocked machines
Modifying system DNS settings via a network card HID
HID attacks triggered when plugged into USB ports
Discoverer: Karsten Nohl and his team at Security Research Labs
Olaf Tan and Dennis Goh of RFID Research Group
Security researcher using Twitter handle MG
Impacted Systems: Devices with USB ports including phones and MacBook chargers
Attack Vector: Malicious USB charging cable plugged into USB ports
Indicators of Compromise: Videos demonstrating USB cables performing HID attacks
Internal images shared between MG and Mitnick
Commands launched on screen on victim machines
